cells.tense: A fair account of what is owed runs quietly under the day.
cells.ask: Go back over one change you lived through — a job that ended, a habit you set down — and spend half an hour naming what it actually left you. Not what you wanted. What's in your hands now.
cells.core:
You can look at something that ended or changed and read the account without flinching. There is a fair sense of what is owed that runs under the day, and in this place it is clear enough to trust. You can feel which part of a situation carries the weight without having the reason in hand, and you can move on it anyway. That is the good version, and it is the one operating.

Behind you there is fruit you likely have not picked up — things a change grew while you were busy being correct about something else. Set aside half an hour this week and take stock of a single ending: what it produced in you, what it cost, what it taught. Don't improve the tally while you look at it. Look, and then stop looking. You'll find more in the pile than your own count allowed for.
cells.sheetLine: You can read what changed without needing to know why.
cells.verb: weighing what is owed against what is

cells.tense: The fairness check is already running on what has not happened yet.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: Whose load is heavy right now? Carry one concrete piece of it — a ride, a meal, an afternoon of your hands — and set it down finished, with no lesson tied to it.
cells.core:
The sense of fairness is running ahead of events, weighing what will be owed before anything has occurred. It reads as responsibility, and it may look that way to anyone standing nearby. From where you sit, it is a steady hum of what is about to be unfair, and it does not switch off when the day does. A check that should land on facts is landing on forecast instead.

Fairness also moves, not only balances. Let some of what you have go toward a load that is current and real. One errand, half an afternoon, no payback ledger attached and no teaching packed inside. That is the whole move. With the weight off your own books for an hour, you'll hear how much of the hum was only the pre-weighing.
cells.sheetLine: The check is running on a bill that hasn't come.

cells.tense: You felt what mattered before and do not stand in that room now.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Name one place where the next step is plain to you, then walk it yourself this week, and tell no one you did. Just the movement, done by you, once.
cells.core:
You can look at a situation and feel which part of it weighs more, without working for the feeling. That read has gone quiet. What reaches you now is the residue — the second-guessing, the re-checking, the sense that the important part of anything cannot be located. The compass has not gone anywhere. It has been crowded out of the room where the calls get made.

Your own tally is crediting you with less than you have. Find one thing, small, where the direction is plain, and take the step — a call, a decision, an errand you have been circling. Not for anyone else and not as an example. Just the movement, done by you, once. Knowing what to attend to comes back through the feet as much as through the head.
cells.sheetLine: The reading hasn't gone — it's stopped being consulted.

cells.tense: The calls are being made all day and filed under circumstance.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Take three things you believe matter, and for each ask whether you arrived at it or took it on. One line per item saying where it came from. Keep the ones that are yours.
cells.core:
You read situations fast and accurately, and the reading gets dismissed as what anyone would think. The calls land, the perceptions hold, and no name goes on the judgment — not even for you. Alongside your own sense of what is fair there are older ones in the mix, taken up from a parent, an employer, a loyalty whose debt is paid.

Take three things you believe matter. For each, ask whether you arrived at it or absorbed it, and write a single line about where it came from. Not to throw anything out — to see which pulls are actually yours. Most people find one clear owner and two inherited. Knowing which is which, you stop paying interest on debts you did not sign.
cells.sheetLine: You've been signing for standards you did not choose.
